prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” roofing company for every homeowner — the right choice depends on your needs (budget, roof material, warranty, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, timeline, location inside Dallas, etc.). I can help you find the best fit. To start, here’s a quick guide so you can pick a top-quality roofer and avoid common pitfalls — and if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood I’ll pull a short vetted list of local companies.

What to look for in a roofer
- Local experience and reputation in Dallas (not a transient storm-chaser).  
- Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Platinum, CertainTeed SELECT, etc.). Those mean the roofer can offer enhanced manufacturer warranties.  
- Proof of insurance: general liability and worker’s comp (or signed indemnity if they don’t carry WC). Ask for a current Certificate of Insurance.  
- Written warranty: separate manufacturer (shingle) warranty and contractor workmanship warranty (length and terms).  
- Proper permitting and code knowledge for City of Dallas inspections.  
- References and recent job photos; check Google Reviews, BBB, and homeowner sites.  
- Clear written estimate with scope, materials, cleanup, permit fees, timeline, payment schedule, and change-order policy.

How to vet estimates
- Get at least 3 written estimates. Compare scope (teardown vs overlay), materials, underlayment, venting, flashing, drip edge, ice/water shield, and disposal.  
- Beware very low bids — could mean shortcuts or missing insurance.  
- Don’t pay full up front. Typical schedule: small deposit, progress payment(s), balance at completion and after you receive lien releases.

Red flags
- High-pressure sales tactics or demand for full cash up front.  
- No local address or unable/unwilling to provide references.  
- Contractor won’t sign a written contract or provide insurance certificates.  
- Offers only “storm special” prices without proper permits or inspections.

Where to check credentials and reviews
- Google Reviews / Yelp / Angi / Houzz.  
- Better Business Bureau (BBB).  
- Manufacturer locator pages (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) to find certified contractors.  
- City of Dallas permit records (to see past permits/inspections).

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short vetted list of 3–5 Dallas-area roofers if you share your ZIP code or neighborhood.  
- Give an inspection checklist to use when they come estimate.  
- Help compare 2–3 written estimates you receive.

Which would you like to do next?
